propositions: A transient git fetch timeout from the GitHub mirror is converted to SnapshotFetchError, caught by adapter's blanket exception handler, and classified as review-error rather than retryable infrastructure fault.
The adapter returns a BLOCK decision on review-error, voter maps it to LLM-Review -1 vote, and writes a dedup row, removing the change from backfill's re-eligibility filter.
Backfill reconciler pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote and already_voted, so a change with a spurious -1 is never re-reviewed even after the transient fault clears.
The fix distinguishes retryable infrastructure faults (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) and returns ABSTAIN without voting or writing dedup rows.
An abstained change remains vote-less and is re-picked by backfill on the next pass, restoring self-healing for transient network faults.
The voter emits VOTER_ERROR marker for abstained reviews so infrastructure timeouts are still observable in metrics, matching the outer no-vote safety net already present in app.py and reconcile.py.
